prTitle: feat(cdc/consents): refactor consent data extraction with deep search functionality

analysis.summary: The refactor introduces breaking API contract changes by renaming response fields and changing data types, while also causing a functional regression by replacing descriptive consent names with technical object paths.

bugs.title: Breaking API Change: Response Property Renaming and Type Mismatch
bugs.description: The response properties 'Name' in both 'subscriptions' and 'preferences' arrays were renamed to 'name'. Additionally, 'isSubscribed' and 'isConsentGranted' changed from strings (joined by '') to direct boolean values (or undefined).
bugs.risk: Downstream consumers (mobile/web apps) expecting 'Name' will receive undefined, and strictly-typed integrations expecting string values for statuses will crash or fail to process the new boolean types.
bugs.codeSnippet:
([key, value]: [string, any]) => ({
-            Name: key,
-            isSubscribed: deepFind(value, `isSubscribed`)
+            name: key,
+            isSubscribed: deepFind(value, `isSubscribed`)[0],

bugs.title: Functional Regression: Loss of Descriptive Consent Names
bugs.description: The logic for consent names was changed from extracting human-readable values from 'customData' (using extractNameFromCustomData) to using technical JSON object paths (e.g., 'services.marketing').
bugs.risk: This will cause the UI to display technical property keys instead of descriptive labels (e.g., showing 'terms.tos' instead of 'Terms of Service'), which is a significant degradation of the user experience.

notBugs.reason: The change from .join('') to [0] for isSubscribed is a logic simplification. While it changes the behavior for multiple values or empty arrays (returning undefined instead of an empty string), it is likely intended in a refactor focusing on specific node extraction.
